subject.title: feat: add linux/riscv64 Docker image to multi-platform build

question: Should OpenClaw officially publish and maintain a best-effort standalone linux/riscv64 Docker image through its release workflow?
rationale: This adds a supported release artifact with recurring CI, supply-chain, documentation, and operator expectations; implementation correctness alone cannot establish that support commitment.

options.title: Sponsor standalone image
options.body: Accept an architecture-suffixed, non-blocking image that cannot alter or delay existing amd64 and arm64 artifacts or release gates.

options.title: Keep community-maintained
options.body: Decline an official artifact and leave riscv64 images externally maintained until upstream base-image and native-dependency support matures.

recommendation.title: Sponsor standalone image
recommendation.body: Accept an architecture-suffixed, non-blocking image that cannot alter or delay existing amd64 and arm64 artifacts or release gates.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across Docker release orchestration, runtime images, and artifact-validation boundaries.
